_contract: Hosts Civitas does not read automatically because their owner told Civitas so directly (owner policy, 2026-10-29: notice and stop). Public election records are read openly from every other site, identified, signed and paced (/about/crawler), and Civitas stops when a site blocks it (crawl_policy) or asks it to stop (an entry here). A site's terms-of-use boilerplate alone does not put it here. crawl_policy refuses every request to a listed host before it is sent (TermsForbid), from every reader, the link check, the source crawl and the data refresh's scripts, and the source map says why. A host matches its own name and every name under it, unless the entry sets "subdomains": false. Each entry says who asked and when (`asked`) and quotes the site's terms; `text_sha256` is the hash of the terms around `quote` as reviewed (app/host_terms_check.page_text from `reviewed_capture`), which the weekly check (host_terms_check) compares with the Internet Archive's newest capture, alerting on a change. A host leaves this file only when its owner allows Civitas in, in writing (record that here).

mi-boe.entellitrak.com.quote: You specifically agree not to access, or attempt to access, or allow any employee, agent, or contractor to access or attempt to access any of the website through any automated means (including, but not limited to, use of scripts, web crawlers or screen scrapers)
mi-boe.entellitrak.com.why: The Bureau of Elections' Candidate Listing Report, a state government information system with no terms of its own; the Department of State's policies cover the state's systems.
mi-boe.entellitrak.com.asked: The Department of State denied Civitas's written request for permission to read its sites automatically (2026-10-28) and referred Civitas to the Voting Information Project.
